reason: A keeps the original's stack (logo, can, headline, CTA, legal at the foot) with even spacing and a strong headline and CTA. Its flaws are minor: the top-right circle now sits mostly inside the canvas instead of bleeding off the edge, and the legal line is very small. B has more problems. The big teal circle now sits behind both the GLACIER logo and the can, so the brand mark loses its clean ground. The can is shrunk and the headline is tight against the CTA. The legal line floats over the bottom-left circle with a dead band of empty space beneath it.

A is a clean banner: the bottle sits on the yellow circle at left and a centred stack of wordmark, headline, subtitle and CTA follows a clear order. Its flaws are a very small subtitle at banner size and an empty green circle at right that adds weight but no content. B is jammed: the headline is oversized, nearly touches the bottle and runs into the circles at right, which now overlap each other in a muddy cluster. B's wordmark is also stranded at the far left, away from the bottle, the subtitle wraps into a cramped three-line block, and the CTA is pushed against the right edge, so nothing breathes and the brand stops reading as one unit.

A drops the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow, sets the body copy almost as large as the headline, and shrinks the 'Reserve a Case' button to an unreadable chip squeezed beside the legal text in a cramped right column. That buries the CTA and breaks the hierarchy. B keeps the original order (eyebrow, headline, divider, body, prominent CTA, ships note, legal) on a centred axis. It still needs work: the header band and logo are tiny, the body copy is small, and the legal text sits jammed near the bottom edge.

A: the headline runs almost to the right edge with no margin, the subtitle and logo start at a different left edge from the headline, and the CTA floats on its own at mid-right. The flavour pills sit below the CTA in a separate band, which breaks the reading order and leaves the layout looking scattered. B: one clean left column (logo, two-line headline, subtitle, pills, CTA) with good hierarchy, and the peach circle balances the right side. Minor flaws: the right half feels a little empty, and the pill labels are small.

A has a clear left-to-right flow (brand, headline, details and CTA, product) with a prominent RSVP button. Its flaws: the logo is tiny and nearly invisible, the 'FREEENTRY' chip text is cramped, the legal line and the missing-asset placeholder are jammed against the bottom edge, and the product sits in a cropped circle. B is fragmented: the RSVP is shrunk into a chip that looks like the other tags and is buried, the subhead floats between the headline and the date with a large gap under the date, the legal text is tiny and crowded into the right corner, and the product is shoved into the top-right corner.

A shrinks the three plan cards into tiny chips whose MONTHLY/YEARLY/FAMILY labels and 'per month' text can't be read. It also reorders them (6, 80, 48), moving the featured yearly plan to the end, and crams the subhead and legal copy into a ragged block on the right edge that is nearly as prominent as the message. B keeps the cards readable, in their original order and with all their labels, and gives the CTA a clear place. However, B's headline is too small for the hero, the subhead and legal text are very small, and the logo, headline and cards sit unevenly on the vertical axis, so it needs polish before it could ship.

A shrinks the circles back inside the canvas so the GLACIER wordmark and the top of the can sit on the big teal circle, which breaks the clean backdrop the original had. A also leaves a large empty band at the top and a dead zone under the legal line, and the legal line floats mid-canvas over the light-blue circle. B keeps the original structure: the circles bleed off the corners, the logo sits on clean background, the can is a good size, the spacing from headline to CTA to legal is even, and the legal line is anchored at the bottom. B's only flaw is legal text that is tiny at this size, and A has the same problem.

A is jammed: the headline touches the top edge and its 'fizz' runs into the overlapping circles, the CTA pill nearly touches the right and bottom edges, the bottle is clipped at the top and bottom, and the body copy wraps into a cramped three-line block, so the strip reads as packed with no margins. B keeps the original's centred stack (logo, headline, body, CTA) with the bottle on its peach circle, so it stays clean and on brand, but the body copy and CTA label are tiny at this size, the bottle runs edge to edge, and the large green circle on the right leaves dead space.

A keeps the original top-to-bottom order with a strong headline and clear orange CTA. But the header band is squeezed so the SOLSTICE logo is almost invisible, the body copy is tiny, and the legal block at the bottom is as large as the body text and crowds the edge. B buries the CTA as a tiny pill, while the bottom-left body paragraph is set larger than anything but the headline, so the hierarchy is inverted. B's legal text and 'Ships late June' are unreadably small in a cramped right column, which makes the bottom half look lopsided and arbitrary.

A is a clean left-aligned stack. Logo, headline, subhead, pills and CTA share one left edge, the hierarchy is clear and the brand circles survive. Its flaws are the tiny pill labels and a somewhat empty right half filled only by the peach circle. B's headline runs almost into the right edge, and the logo, headline and subhead start at slightly different left positions. The CTA floats on the right, cut off from the text column, and the flavour pills sit below it at the bottom, which breaks the reading order. The peach circle is a cramped fragment jammed into the top-right corner.

A shrinks the RSVP CTA to a pill the same size as the three badges and lines them up in one row, so the call to action gets lost. It also breaks the headline over two lines and squeezes the italic subhead into a narrow, cramped column. The logo is mangled ('SOLST CE'), the legal text is jammed into the right corner, and the columns don't line up. B has a clear left-to-right order: headline block, then date/badges/a large RSVP button, then the product in its circle. Its flaws are a tiny, illegible logo, a missing-asset placeholder that runs off the bottom-right corner, and a sun circle cropped hard at the right edge.

A keeps the plans in the original order (Monthly, Yearly, Family) and the price cards are readable, with a clear left-to-right flow ending at the CTA. But the cards nearly touch the top and bottom edges, the headline is too small to lead over the cards, the logo is pushed into a cramped left margin, and the legal text is tiny. B makes the price cards so small that their labels and per-month copy can't be read, swaps the order to 6/80/48 so Yearly comes last, and jams the cards against the CTA. Its subtitle and legal text are crammed into the right edge, with the legal text running to the bottom, and the oversized headline dwarfs the actual offer.

A fills the tall format well: the pack is large, the headline is big but breaks onto two lines ('Garden-fresh / fizz', a slightly weak break), and the green circle still sits behind the pack as in the original. Its flaws are that the CTA is jammed tight under the headline and there is some dead space at the bottom. B looks like a shrunk copy: the CITRINE logo and the 'Find a Store' button text are undersized, there is a large empty gap between the logo and the pack, the green circle drifts off on its own in the corner instead of layering behind the pack, and the elements float small in the middle of the canvas.

A: the headline clearly dominates and the CTA sits top-right, but the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is jammed into the bottom-left corner below the logo, the product is tiny, and the legal copy is squeezed into a three-line column under the CTA that runs into the bottom edge and a background dot. B: the SOLSTICE logo is shrunk onto a dark planet disc and is nearly unreadable, the sale ribbon sits on top of another planet, and the headline is smaller and crowded between the ribbon and the CTA with a stray dot beside it. B's one-line legal text is cleaner, but losing the brand mark is the worse flaw.

A shrinks everything: the CITRINE logo and the 'Find a Store' label become tiny, the content sits in a small band in the middle with dead space above and below, and the green circle is pushed off to the side instead of sitting behind the bag as in the original. B keeps the original layering (green circle behind the bag), enlarges the bag, logo and CTA to suit the tall format and fills the height better, but the headline wraps to leave 'fizz' alone on the second line, the gap between headline and button is tight, and the olive circle crowds the bottom-left.

A reads cleanly left to right (brand, can, ribbon, headline, CTA) with the CTA vertically centred, but the SOLSTICE logo is shrunk to an illegible mark inside a dark planet circle, the can is tiny, and there is a dead gap between the can and the ribbon, which sits awkwardly on the planet. B runs the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon off the bottom-left canvas edge, crams the can and logo into the top-left corner, and wraps the legal text into a 3-line block under the CTA that is jammed against the bottom edge, so the right-hand column is top-heavy and cramped.

A reads cleanly left to right (product, then headline and copy, then badge and CTA) and keeps the product as a real visual. Its flaws: the SOLSTICE logo is tiny, the tilted sale badge is undersized and crowds the right edge, the legal line floats far below the copy, and the right column is noticeably narrower than the left. B makes the product a trivial thumbnail lost in the top-right corner over the planet circle. Its oversized headline jams against the bottom edge, the badge floats in the middle with no anchor, and the right column (copy, CTA, legal) is cramped against a heavy left side, so the original's product-centred feel is lost.

A reflows the headline into four large, well-broken lines that fill the square and dominate. However, the bottom row splits the centred axis: the centre-aligned three-line subcopy sits ragged in a left column (its edges don't match the headline's) beside an off-centre CTA, so the base looks improvised. B is a clean, faithful centred stack, but it's essentially the banner scaled up: the headline runs almost edge to edge (~50px margins), the subcopy is one long line nearly touching the sides, and wide empty orange bands sit above and below, so it doesn't use the square format.

A keeps the original reading order (eyebrow, headline, body, product, CTA). The circle is redrawn as a deliberate backdrop behind the bottle. Its flaws are small: the body copy breaks awkwardly, leaving 'sparkling.' alone on a line; the centred bottle and circle sit off the left text axis; and there is a slightly loose gap above the CTA. B moves 'WEEKEND ONLY' below the body copy, which breaks the eyebrow-to-headline order. Its headline is jammed against the cropped circle in the top-right corner. Its text is left-aligned while the bottle and CTA are centred, so the axes are mixed. The CTA is bigger than it needs to be, and the bottom has dead space.

A: the phone and its backing circle are jammed against the left edge, the circle is cut off there, and the CTA sits cramped in the bottom-right corner (about 13 px from the bottom). The badge and button are pushed into a lower row and float apart from the headline block, so the layout looks crowded with an empty upper-right area. B: a clean three-column banner (phone, centred headline and subcopy, badge stacked over the CTA) with even margins and the original's reading order kept. The headline is a bit small for the canvas, the subcopy is thin, and the phone is somewhat oversized relative to the text.

A uses the tall canvas better and keeps the type larger. However, it shrinks the hero sun circle into a small corner blob, which loses the original's feel. It also leaves a dead gap of about 110 px between the subhead and the date block, and the partner mark sits jammed against the bottom-right edge. B keeps the circle at the original's scale and the original's header-over-circle layering. But it squeezes the whole block into the middle at a smaller size, so the badges and URL line become very small. The partner mark floats in the middle of the bottom area, with a band of dead space at the bottom of about 120 px. Both are just shrunk copies of the square layout, not real portrait rearrangements.

A: the bottle has shrunk to a thumbnail jammed into the top-right corner, so the main product image is lost. The legal line is the same size as the offer copy, and the oversized headline crowds the bottom-left edge while the right column is cramped. B keeps the bottle as a large focal point and reads left to right (bottle, headline, CTA), but the SOLSTICE logo is tiny, the stretched-out sale ribbon is jammed against the right edge, and the bottle nearly touches the bottom of the canvas.

A keeps the original's centred stack intact: headline, subcopy, then CTA, with clear hierarchy and balanced space above and below. Its flaws are that the headline and subcopy run almost edge to edge with only about 50px side margins, and the block reads as the banner scaled up rather than recomposed for a square. B's oversized four-line headline is bold, but the subcopy and CTA are squeezed into a side-by-side row at the bottom. That subcopy is centre-aligned and wraps into three ragged lines that line up with nothing, the CTA is pushed off the central axis, and the row sits cramped against the bottom edge while the headline takes up most of the canvas.

A breaks reading order: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow drops below the body copy. The left-aligned text block also clashes with the centred bottle and centred CTA, and the cropped circle sits behind the headline in no clear way. B keeps the original order: eyebrow, headline, copy, product, CTA. Its text and CTA share one left edge, and the circle now frames the bottle on purpose. Its remaining flaws are small: the circle is slightly off-centre, and the gaps below the circle and under the CTA are a little large.

A keeps the original's left-to-right banner order (phone in circle, then headline and subline centred vertically, then the ONLINE ONLY badge stacked over the Try It button), with even margins and a clear hierarchy. Its flaws are that the headline is a little small for the canvas and there is a wide empty gap between the copy and the CTA column. B makes the headline bigger but crowds it against the top edge and pushes the badge and CTA into the bottom-right corner almost touching the bottom edge. That leaves dead space under the subline on the left, and the phone and circle are cut off at the left edge, so the layout looks cramped and lopsided.

A is basically the square shrunk into the middle of the taller canvas: about 100px of dead space above the logo, a big empty band of dots under the partner placeholder, smaller headline, badges and CTA, and the large circle now runs into the logo and header area. B fills the height better, with the header near the top and a larger headline, badges and CTA, and it keeps the partner mark in the bottom-right corner like the original. Its flaws: a dead gap of about 120px between the subtitle and the date block, the event block hugging the left at x≈63 off the centred axis, and the circle shrunk into a minor corner blob.

A reads cleanly from left to right in the leaderboard format: phone with its circle, then brand, a one-line headline and the tagline, then the badges stacked together and the CTA. Its flaws are the phone squeezed small and clipped at the bottom of the canvas, the badges sitting a bit loose in the middle, and a CTA almost touching the right edge. B is cramped and jumbled: SOLSTICE floats on its own to the left of a headline that wraps to two lines, the CTA is jammed under a badge in a tight cluster with the SUMMER ONLY badge left alone at top right, the right side and gaps are dead space, and the phone is clipped at the top and bottom.

A is a clean top-to-bottom story: headline, product centred on its purple circle (kept as a deliberate backdrop), CTA, then fine print, all sharing one left edge. Its flaws are minor: the CTA sits a long way below the copy, and there is a large dead gap above the bottom legal line. B has collided the purple circle with the headline, so 'WEEKEND ONLY' and '20% off' sit half on and half off the blob. The text is blown up so large that '20% off' and the CTA crowd the right edge. The product floats with no circle behind it, and the legal line is oversized, almost competing with the message.

A rearranges the design well (bottle in its circle as the hero, then headline, then the NEW + Try It row), but the headline is left-offset (starts ~x=85) and is not centred on the axis the bottle and buttons share. The headline is also fairly small for the square, and the lone faint circle in the top left looks like a stray. B pushes the bottle into the top-left corner with its cap almost touching the canvas edge and its decorative circle cropped. The NEW pill is blown up to nearly CTA size so the two compete, the stacked right-aligned buttons leave the bottom left dead, and the product is shrunk to an afterthought next to the oversized headline.

A: SOLSTICE is pushed beside the headline rather than above it, there's a dead gap between the phone and the text, and the badges are stacked in a 2x2 grid at the same size as the CTA. That makes 'Find It Near You' read as just another pill, and the empty right third leaves the layout lopsided. B reads left to right in the right order (brand, headline, badges, CTA) with a clear one-line headline and a dominant CTA. But the CTA nearly touches the right edge, the gap between the text and the badges is wide, and the stacked badges are large next to the small subline.

A: the oversized '20% off' runs almost to the right edge and sits on the cropped purple circle, which is now cut off from the product it framed; the product floats alone in a large empty lower area, the full-width CTA is cramped under the subhead, and the legal line is nearly as big as the subhead, which flattens the hierarchy. B: clean left-aligned stack (eyebrow, headline, subhead), the product is properly centred in its circle, and it reads headline, then product, then CTA. Its flaws are minor: the 'Ends Sunday' legal text is very small and low-contrast, and the CTA leaves dead space to its right.

A: the bottle badge is crammed into the top-left corner with its cap poking out of the circle near the canvas edge. The NEW pill is nearly as big as the CTA and stacked right-aligned against the left-aligned headline, so the two blocks don't line up. The bottom-left is left as a big dead area, which makes the layout lopsided. B: the centered stack (bottle hero, then headline, then the NEW/Try It row) suits the square format, but the headline is about 50 px left of the shared center axis and small next to the oversized bottle. The faint decor circle in the top-left is stranded, but nothing collides and the hierarchy and reading order hold.
